**Step 1:** First, we write the inverse function implicitly. The given function is $y=3{x}^{3}+9x,$ and to write the inverse function implicitly, we swap $x$ and $y$ as follows:

$$
x=3{y}^{3}+9y
$$

Note that in the equation above, we have $y={f}^{-1}(x).$

**Step 2:** Next, we differentiate. The overall goal is to find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x},$ but the equation is already solved for $x,$ so we compute $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y}$ and then take the reciprocal:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(3{y}^{3}+9y) \\ \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y} & =9{y}^{2}+9 \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{1}{9{y}^{2}+9}\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 3:** Lastly, we write the result in terms of ${f}^{-1}(x).$ Since $y={f}^{-1}(x),$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}[{f}^{-1}(x)] & =\frac{1}{9{({f}^{-1}(x))}^{2}+9} \\ {({f}^{-1})}^{′}(x) & =\frac{1}{9{({f}^{-1}(x))}^{2}+9}.\end{aligned}
$$
